title: Giant Greenland Iceberg Collides with Island and Drifts Onward
seoTitle: Giant Greenland iceberg collides and persists
subtitle: Ice mass over 76 km² broke off in 2026 and is being tracked by satellites.
excerpt: A colossal iceberg, covering more than 76 square kilometers, broke off the Petermann Glacier in Greenland in August 2026.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
A notable Arctic event occurred in August 2026 when a colossal iceberg broke away from the Petermann Glacier in Greenland. Covering an area of over 76 square kilometers, this was the largest glacier calving in the Arctic region since 2020.

The massive ice sheet, after detaching from the glacier, began a drifting journey. At one point, the iceberg collided with Joe Island. Despite the impact, the ice structure showed remarkable resilience, remaining intact and not fragmenting.

Currently, the iceberg is under constant monitoring. Satellites track its movement as it continues its course through the Nares Strait. The trajectory of this ice giant is being closely observed as it advances across the region.

With information from ScienceDaily.
